fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.schema_description: Location containing the devices to update.

options.notes: From useEnvData siteData (useEnvData.ts:34-41). The UI value is 'dcim-location:["<location_type>","<id>"]' when the row has location_type (location-options.ts:21-36). location_type is a repeated static query param.

fields.query_param_normalization: Uses the query param 'location', not 'site'. It is set only when it resolves against loaded locations (by encoded value, id, or display name; :144-145). An unresolvable value is not cleared: the raw query string stays in the field from defaultValues (:303) and is submitted as-is.
fields.submit_transform: The encoded option is decoded: location = option id, or the raw value if no option matches. The location type is emitted as location_type (:374-378).

fields.name: roles
fields.label: Roles
fields.schema_description: Device roles used to filter the selected network devices.
fields.query_param_normalization: Multi-value (getAll('role'), singular name). The field is replaced with the valid subset only if at least one value matches a loaded option key. If none match, the raw query values stay from defaultValues (:305) and are submitted (:115-129).
fields.submit_transform: Array sent as-is. Each value is also sent as a repeated 'role' param on the device lookup that feeds the secret options.

fields.name: status
fields.label: Device Status
fields.schema_description: Device statuses used to filter the selected network devices.
fields.query_param_normalization: Multi-value (getAll('status')). The default is the raw query values when any are present (:306); they are replaced by the valid subset only if at least one matches (:115-129). Invalid values are not cleared.
client_only_validation: At least one item: 'Device Status is required' (:53-56)
fields.submit_transform: Array sent as-is. It is also sent as repeated 'status' params on the device lookup.

fields.name: tenant
fields.label: Tenant
fields.schema_description: Tenant used to filter the selected network devices.
fields.query_param_normalization: Single value. Set to the option value only if it matches a loaded option key; an invalid value stays as the raw query string from defaultValues (:103-113, :307).
fields.submit_transform: '' becomes undefined, so the key is omitted (:382). It is also sent as a 'tenant' param on the device lookup.

fields.name: selected_secret
fields.label: Secret to Rotate
fields.schema_description: Name of the managed secret containing the replacement password.

options.notes: Chained lookup. useDevices runs with buildDeviceFilterParams(location, roles, status, tenant) (:161-177, :317-324), and the first returned device id (getFirstDeviceId :179-187) is put in the path (getPasswordUsersUrl :189-200). There is no request until that device exists. The endpoint returns {name: <username>, description: '<username> (<secret_name>)'} (parameter_v1.py:409-433); the UI uses name for both label and value (mapSecretOptions :202-215).

fields.query_param_normalization: Read into defaultValues (:304), but the effect at :347-349 unconditionally sets selected_secret to '' after the first render (and on every location/roles/status/tenant change), so the query value does not survive.
client_only_validation: Disabled until at least one matching device exists (:473)
Label text changes with state: '(select location first)', '(loading devices...)', '(no matching devices)', '(loading secrets...)', '(no secrets found)' (getSecretLabel :217-240)

fields.name: location_type
fields.schema_description: DCIM location type for the location identifier.
fields.widget_today: none (derived from the selected location option)
fields.submit_transform: location.locationType of the resolved option (:378). The key is omitted when undefined.

payload_transform: onSubmit (site-password-rotation-workflow-form.tsx:372-404) builds {location: option?.id ?? data.location, location_type: option?.locationType, selected_secret, roles, status, tenant: data.tenant || undefined} and POSTs it to /v1/workflow/ngc/site_password_rotation; undefined keys are dropped by JSON.stringify. On success it toasts 'Workflow Started' and calls form.reset(), although startWorkflow has already set location.href to the run page. The DeviceMatchStatus element ('Found N matching devices', :242-283, rendered at :461-465) is display-only.
discrepancies: The selected_secret schema description says 'Name of the managed secret containing the replacement password', but the UI submits the password-user username (password_users row 'name'). The workflow passes it on as username (device_password_rotation.py:353-361), so the description does not match the submitted value.
Secret options come only from the first matching device, so password users that exist only on other matching devices are not offered.
The selected_secret query param is effectively ignored because the clearing effect runs after mount (:347-349).
Invalid location/role/status/tenant query values are not cleared and are submitted raw. The site backup and cable validation forms clear them instead.
The location prefill uses the query param 'location', while every other site-scoped form uses 'site'.
The UI requires at least one status; the schema allows an empty list.
Label 'Device Status' differs from schema title 'Status'; label 'Secret to Rotate' differs from title 'Selected Secret'.
Spec coverage is minimal: sitePasswordRotationForm.spec.ts has no payload, query-param or error-path tests.
contract_gaps: The selected_secret OptionSource needs a path-templated endpoint (/v1/parameter/device/{id}/password_users) whose id comes from another option query (the first device matching location/roles/status/tenant). OptionSource has no path templating and no chained or derived lookups. A server-side query-param endpoint (for example /v1/parameter/password_users?location=&location_type=&role=&status=&tenant=) would reduce this to a cascade, though it would still need repeated params.
The dependency values for roles/status are arrays sent as repeated query params, and depends_on does not define array handling.
location_type is a sibling filled from the selected location option's location_type ('<field>_type' convention, workflow_submission.py:163); this is not in the contract.
There is no hint for state-dependent label text or for the 'Found N matching devices' status line.
The disabled-until-dependency-resolves behaviour and the clearing of selected_secret on any filter change are unspecified.
The location option source needs the repeated static param location_type=Site&location_type=Module.
